standard_prerequisites.name: Galois closure of a finite separable extension
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Fields, the lemma that the normal closure of a finite separable extension is Galois, and the lemma that a Galois extension of a Galois extension remains Galois
standard_prerequisites.use: Allows replacing the top field by its Galois closure over the base.

standard_prerequisites.name: Splitting of the tensor product of a finite Galois extension
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: The decomposition of the tensor product of a finite Galois extension of a field with a field between the base and the extension into a product indexed by the Galois group
standard_prerequisites.use: Produces the isomorphism between the disjoint union of copies of the spectrum of the top field and the product of the spectra, and hence the induced isomorphism on cohomology.

core_obligations: Replace by the Galois closure (proof lines 5306-5313): the top field may be replaced by its normal closure over the base, which is Galois over the base and over the intermediate field, since the statement only becomes stronger.

Split the product (proof lines 5313-5325): the tensor product of the intermediate field with the Galois extension splits as a product indexed by the Galois group of the extension over the intermediate field, which exhibits the product of the two spectra as a disjoint union of copies of the spectrum of the top field.

Conclude injectivity (proof lines 5325-5333): the induced isomorphism on cohomology displays an element of the tensor product as the tuple of its pullbacks capped with the pullbacks along the automorphisms; taking the second factor to be one shows that an element mapping to zero must already be zero.
proof_roadmap: Replace the top field by its Galois closure.
Split the product of the spectra using the tensor product decomposition.
Read off injectivity from the induced cohomological isomorphism.
difficulty_reason: The lemma proves that for data satisfying the first seven axioms the cohomology in degree zero of the spectrum of an intermediate finite separable extension injects into that of the larger extension (statement lines 5302-5307). The proof (proof lines 5308-5333) replaces the top field by its Galois closure and splits the product of the two spectra into copies of the spectrum of the top field. H2: a complete short argument in two steps.
